entries.proposition: Scope: a narrative review of MAMs in neurodegeneration, with no search method or appraisal stated.
entries.snippet: This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the structural and functional characteristics of MAMs and their role in the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases.

entries.proposition: Disease coverage is Alzheimer, Parkinson, ALS and Huntington disease only; no developmental, epileptic or inherited-metabolic disorder is covered (the words epilepsy, seizure, ferroptosis and iron do not occur in the article, counted in this session).
entries.snippet: This section highlights how MAM impairment manifests in four major neurodegenerative disorders—AD, PD, ALS, and HD—emphasizing the shared and disease-specific alterations

entries.proposition: Section 3 summary: MAM changes are increased tethering in AD and reduced connectivity in PD and ALS.
entries.snippet: through increased tethering (e.g., in AD), reduced connectivity (e.g., in PD and ALS), or structural interference by mutant proteins (e.g., in HD)

entries.proposition: Parkinson section, first statement: PINK1 and Parkin loss reduces ER-mitochondria tethering and calcium exchange.
entries.snippet: reduce ER–mitochondria tethering and calcium exchange, thereby impairing mitochondrial ATP production

entries.proposition: Parkinson section, second statement: PARK2-mutant fibroblasts and Parkin knock-out mice show ER and mitochondria in closer proximity, more calcium flow and more MFN2, the opposite direction from the summary and from the previous sentence.
entries.snippet: the ER and mitochondria were in proximity together, Ca2+ flow to the cytosol increased, and MFN2 (which is implicated in ER–mitochondria tethering) increased [62]

entries.proposition: Lipid droplets: MAMs described as LD nucleation sites and excess LDs seen in AD, ALS and HD models; no mitochondrial-disease LD material (compare the OXPHOS-deficiency paper in this lot).
entries.snippet: Excessive or persistent LD accumulation can signify metabolic dysfunction and is observed in AD, ALS, and HD models
entries.anchor: 4.3 Role in Lipid Droplet Formation and Turnover

entries.proposition: Therapy: one peptide, small-molecule and natural-compound lists; the clinical trials in Table 3 are curcumin and resveratrol trials with amyloid, atrophy or isoprostane outcomes, not MAM measures.
entries.snippet: TAT-MP1Gly, a cell-permeable peptide that disrupts the interaction between PTPIP51 and VAPB, reducing excessive ER–mitochondria tethering in AD models
entries.anchor: 7.1 Small Molecules and Peptides Targeting MAM Proteins

entries.proposition: Figure 4 legend names three proteins: MFN2, PACS-2 and ATAD3A.
entries.snippet: This schematic illustrates the ER–MAM–mitochondria interface, highlighting three key proteins: MFN2 (mitofusin-2), PACS-2 (Phosphofurin Acidic Cluster Sorting Protein 2), and ATAD3A

entries.proposition: Figure 4 as displayed is a different schematic from its legend: it shows donor-mitochondria transfer routes (tunnelling nanotubes, extracellular vesicles, mitoception), current treatments (antioxidants, chelators, respiratory-complex regulators) and a MAM inset labelled VDAC1, GRP75, Sig-1R, IP3R, RyRs and SERCA; MFN2, PACS-2 and ATAD3A are not labelled.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4: left boxes 'Donor healthy mitochondria' with mechanism of mitochondrial transfer (spontaneous: TNT, EVs, connexin, free mitochondria; artificial: mitoception) and incorporation routes; right 'Current treatments: dietary supplements, synthetic compounds' with sub-bullets antioxidants, ion-specific chelators, regulators of respiratory complexes, drugs to restore dynamics; lower right inset of mitochondrion-ER contact with VDAC1, GRP75, Sig-1R, IP3R, RyR, SERCA and a legend listing ER, MAM, RyRs, VDAC, GRP75, Sig-1R, IP3R and SERCA.

entries.proposition: The authors state that whether MAM changes are compensatory or causative remains unclear.
entries.snippet: The extent to which MAM changes in neurodegeneration are compensatory or causative remains unclear.

entries.proposition: Future directions named are cell types, sex and ageing; development is not among them.
entries.snippet: future research should examine the differences in MAM remodeling across cell types, sexes, and aging stages
